summary: Read the live FUSED section (app/(foyer)/page.tsx L302-587, the id="products" section) against app/globals.css. The wall isn't the fuse — it's that every object inside it renders at the same weight: (1) each stage's description paragraph (.cw-principle__text) is set in the display face at 20-30px, nearly as large as its own headline (.cw-principle__artifact, 28-44px), so two near-equal "headlines" stack per stage before anything recedes; (2) each stage's embedded evidence ledger uses the identical 2px-rule/24px-row/18-22px-name treatment as the section's own standalone closing ledger, so proof reads at the same weight as the pitch, three times over; (3) the closing "The receipts." h3 reuses .cw-secttitle verbatim, which the code's own comment already flags as class-scaled not tag-scaled — it renders exactly as large as "How I work." above it, a second full-size headline inside one <section>; (4) the transition from the three-stage loop into the closing tally is a single unlabeled 56px inline margin, with no size or register change to signal "this is a different kind of thing now." Five patches below: recede the per-stage description to the site's existing body-copy register (.cw-sect-dek's own scale/face), recede the nested-in-stage ledgers to a quieter treatment scoped so the closing ledger and every other page (grepped — .cw-ledger/.cw-lrow render nowhere else) are untouched, add a size-only .cw-secttitle--sub modifier so the closing subhead stops duplicating the section's real headline, and double the pre-closing gap (56px -> 112px, reusing .cw-exits's own 56px unit rather than inventing a number) so the register change is felt in both space and size. Net effect is a real size ladder per stage (headline > body-copy description > evidence-name > micro-mono proof) instead of two headline-weight beats stacked three times, plus one visible pause before the tally. No copy rewritten, no receipt row cut, no figure touched, no fixed color or text-opacity added anywhere (everything is font-size/weight/margin/padding, or a border-color-mix that already exists elsewhere in this same file) — the CONTRAST FIX block and its color:inherit rule are undisturbed. Estimated net effect on the 2898px figure: roughly -250 to -300px from the description/ledger recession, offset by +56px from the added breathing room, for a net reduction plus materially better pacing. On whole-page rhythm: hero 900 / offer 1037 / FUSED ~2650 (post-patch) / ordani 1101 / close 357 — FUSED stays the tallest section (it is genuinely carrying the most information, and the operator explicitly locked the fuse), but the 3x-any-other-section gap narrows meaningfully without cutting a word. I did not touch .cw-block's 130px section padding (shared by four other sections, already has a documented mobile step-down at L4848) or move anything between sections — out of scope for "de-density the fused section," and moving Ordani/Two-doors is a page-structure call, not a pacing fix, so I left it for a human call if wanted.

Grepped .cw-ledger/.cw-lrow across the whole app+components tree and confirmed they render in exactly four places, all inside this one page.tsx file (three nested in .cw-principle, one standalone closing ledger) — so a descendant-selector scope (.cw-principle .cw-ledger) touches only the three nested instances and cannot regress the closing ledger or any other page. Grepped .cw-secttitle usage on the home page and confirmed the h3 at L564 (id="cw-products-title") is the only h3 using that class, so the new modifier class only ever applies there. Checked lib/banned.ts and lib/copy-lint-runner.ts (SCAN_TARGETS includes app/**/*.tsx and it scans raw file content, comments included) before writing any JSX comment text, to make sure nothing I add trips the build-time banned-word gate. Confirmed via grep that 'marginTop: "56px"' and both CSS anchor blocks are unique, verbatim strings in their files. No figure, name, date, row, or word of copy was invented or altered — every patch is font-size/weight/line-height/letter-spacing/margin/padding, plus one border using color-mix(...25%...) that is the same token already used by .cw-lrow's own row divider two lines away, not a new device.

The closing heading duplicated the section's own primary-headline treatment (flagged in the existing code comment); a size-only modifier fixes the hierarchy without touching heading semantics or the aria wiring.

summary: 11 patches across app/(foyer)/services/page.tsx and app/globals.css, all verified against the live repo. (1) Restores the three real packages ($500 Unstick / $2,500 Audit / $7,500 Sprint) as a working Buy-button table on /services itself — the site's only nav-linked pricing page, since /packages has no nav entry — instead of full imported hero cards, because embedding the /packages hero card's cw-pkg-hero__cta and cw-pkg__cta would add 3 more filled pills on top of the page's existing one (W3, globals.css: "each page keeps exactly one filled pill"). The Buy action is real (calls the same createPackageCheckout Stripe action via BuyButton) but restyled as the page's existing underlined-mono secondary grammar via a new button-safe class. (2) Nests the three service blocks inside the Engagements section visually and structurally: wraps them in one .cw-sv-svc-group with a soft internal divider instead of each carrying its own full-strength currentColor rule, adds a connecting line inside the Engagements copy itself ("Pick one, or run all three together") answering the operator's literal "a client can pick all three" point, and tightens the gap between Engagements' close and the group's start from ~140px to ~72px. (3) Addresses "does not compel action" with two structural (not color/opacity) mechanisms per the HARD CONSTRAINT: promotes the 01/02/03 service index from a 12px mono label to a large light-weight display numeral (SIZE+WEIGHT only, zero opacity, zero new color — the exact axe-failure pattern the brief warns against), and the new Packages table itself is a format-shift (prose wall → table) roughly two-thirds of the way into the page's previously undifferentiated block. Every price, name and deliverable description is copied verbatim from PACKAGES_LD in app/(foyer)/packages/page.tsx (grepped, not invented). Zero em-dashes added to rendered copy (confirmed: the page's only rendered em-dash is in Nav.tsx's "Menu —", all others in the file are JS comments). Zero banned words (checked against .claude/brand.json voice.banned). All new copy uses "I"/imperative, no "we".
reasoning:
Investigated the regression first: `git diff c60ea0e..HEAD -- "app/(foyer)/services/page.tsx"` (already known from the brief) plus reading both page.tsx files confirmed Pass-108 deleted the two-doors nav that linked to /packages and left only a single sentence + link in the Objection section. Nav.tsx has no /packages entry at all — /services is the only page in primary nav that could carry pricing, which is why the operator calls the omission "most important."

For problem 1, I read components/BuyButton.tsx and the exact CSS for .cw-pkg__cta / .cw-pkg-hero__cta (background: var(--color-cw-terracotta) / var(--color-cw-espresso), border-radius: 999px — genuine filled pills) against the operator-locked W3 comment in globals.css ("Each page keeps exactly one filled pill (.cw-cta); everything else is this [.cw-mlink]"). Importing the real package cards as-is would violate that locked rule (4 filled pills on one page). So the patch reuses the *component* (real Stripe checkout, not a dead link) but restyles it with a new .cw-sv-table__buy class built from the same reset/hover pattern as the existing .cw-mlink, verified for correct specificity against the existing mobile media-query rules for .cw-sv-table so it doesn't get silently overridden at 760px.

For problem 2, reading the rendered JSX showed the three services are already h3-after-h2 in document order (so the accessibility outline is technically fine) — the actual defect is purely visual: each cw-sv-svc carries its own full-width border-top: 1px solid currentColor and 44-52px padding, making each read as its own full-bleed chapter with no textual tie-back to "Engagements." The fix keeps the semantic structure (still three landmarked <section aria-labelledby> each with their own h3) but (a) adds one explicit connecting sentence inside the Engagements section itself, (b) wraps the three in a group container so only the first keeps the strong opening rule and the two internal dividers go soft (reusing the same color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 22%, transparent) idiom already used elsewhere on this exact page for "this is one list" grammar), and (c) tightens the vertical gap between Engagements' close and the group's start.

For problem 3, I measured the actual CSS values (.cw-sv-svc__num was 12px mono, nearly invisible) and chose to enlarge it into a real structural device using only size/weight, per the HARD CONSTRAINT against opacity/fixed-color on text (I initially drafted an opacity-based ghost-numeral treatment and caught that it would repeat exactly the pattern that caused the 19-axe-failure incident, so I removed opacity entirely and kept only weight 300 vs the title's weight 700 for the visual hierarchy). Bricolage Grotesque is loaded as a variable font (weight: "variable" in lib/fonts.ts) so 300 renders natively, no synthetic-bold risk.

Every fact used (prices, package names, deliverable text, "From $5K a month", the 60-day credit line) was grepped directly from app/(foyer)/packages/page.tsx's PACKAGES_LD object and JSX rather than paraphrased, per the INVENT-NOTHING constraint — the one place I initially paraphrased ("90 minutes" vs "Ninety minutes," dropping the "or the next package" branch of the credit line) I corrected back to the verbatim locked strings once I checked it against the source.

I verified every anchor's uniqueness with targeted greps (some innocent-looking strings like ".cw-sv-open {" and "margin-bottom: 64px;" recur 2-4 times in globals.css) and only used anchors whose full multi-line body is confirmed unique before finalizing this spec.
